version.value: Original (1892) version of the Sérénade, as played by the composer in 1922; performing text not identified
version.note: Wikipedia’s list of the composer’s recordings labels the 4 November 1922 recording the 1892 version, and the 1940 revised version was published only in 1940 (Henle). IMSLP’s page says No. 5 was revised in 1922; the Henle report documents the revised text as Charles Foley’s 1940 edition, so that remark is not followed. Henle also states that the composer’s own recording diverges from the printed notation of the original version in many places. Henle does not identify which composer recording it means; the cited original score is therefore not assumed to be a literal transcript of the 1922 performance.

date.note: DAHR’s approved take 5 is dated 4 November 1922; takes 1–3 were made on 1 November. The Archive filename and the RCA register give the same date for the reissued track.

place.note: DAHR gives New York for every take; no studio is named.

label.note: Victor is the original label; the uploader identifies the 1992 RCA/BMG set as the immediate source of the file.

catalogue.value: Victor 66129 (10-inch single-faced) and Victor 816 (10-inch double-faced, with Bizet’s Minuet); RCA-BMG 09026 61265 2, CD 10 (1992)
catalogue.note: The Victor numbers and the CD set are separately documented. The disc used for the 1992 transfer is not identified.

matrixTakeSides.note: DAHR names the matrix, takes and issues. The link between that take and this digital file rests on the RCA register (which names the matrix and take for the CD track) and the uploader’s CD identification; no waveform or run-out comparison with the disc was made.

credits.value: John Pfeiffer, reissue producer; Ward Marston, disc-to-DAT transfer; André Gauthier, remastering supervisor; Anthony Salvatore, remastering engineer
credits.note: These are the credits printed for the 1992 RCA/BMG set. Their connection to this access file rests on the uploader’s identification of the item as CD 10 of that set. The later ripper and uploader are not named as engineers.

date.note: The set was issued in 1992, but the dates of the disc-to-DAT transfer, the remastering and the later CD extraction are not stated. The Internet Archive upload of 11 October 2025 is not a transfer date.

processing.value: Disc-to-DAT transfer, then digital remastering at BMG/RCA Studios, New York City; the Internet Archive derives its VBR MP3 from an uploaded WAV.
processing.note: The booklet says surface imperfections were reduced without radical removal of all surface noise. It gives no equalisation, pitch-correction, noise-reduction or editing settings, and none is inferred from the audio analysis.

digital.format: VBR MP3 access derivative; the uploaded source is a WAV taken from a 1992 CD reissue of an acoustic disc

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Rachmaninoff died in 1943. This is a territorial term calculation, not worldwide clearance or a statement about any modern edition.

recording.value: US public domain: the issued sound recording was published by 1925 (Victor 66129 and 816, recorded 1922).
recording.note: DAHR’s catalogue records for Victor 66129 and 816 give a publication date of [1922], and an Internet Archive digitisation of Victrola 66129 gives 1922; both are catalogue-derived years, not release days. The 1925 Victor catalogue lists the Serenade (Op. 3, No. 5) coupled with the Minuet from L’Arlésienne, which establishes publication no later than 1925 independently of the session date. The Archive item’s Public Domain Mark is noted but not relied on. The 1992 booklet carries an all-rights-reserved reissue notice: no claim is made that its text, artwork or compilation is public domain, or that any new creative contribution to the mastering is cleared worldwide.

rights.creditLine: Sergei Rachmaninoff, piano — Sérénade, Op. 3 No. 5. Victor 66129 and 816, matrix B-27110 take 5 (New York, 4 November 1922). Digital source: RCA/BMG Complete Recordings (1992), CD 10, via Internet Archive; Public Domain Mark 1.0 is the item’s licence statement.

OCR text consulted against the track listing.

sources.title: Internet Archive 78rpm item: Serenade (Victrola 66129)
sources.locator: Item metadata: Victrola 66129, publication date 1922, acoustic, piano solo (Op. 3, No. 5); a separate digitisation of the disc, not the source of the file used here.

sources.title: 1925 Catalog of Victor Records, Victor Talking Machine Company
sources.locator: Title page: copyright 1925. OCR text of the Red Seal listings; the entries relevant here are named in the recording fields. Contemporary evidence that the record was on sale by 1925, independent of the session date. Entry relevant here: “Minuet—Rachmaninoff Piano and Serenade (Op.3) Rachmaninoff”, i.e. the Victor 816 coupling.

sources.locator: Four pages of the 1892 version: Sostenuto, Tempo di Valse, closing ppp–pppp chords and final ff chord with fermata. Used for form and markings only; the performing edition is not identified.

sources.title: U.S. Copyright Office: Classics Protection and Access Act
sources.locator: Term section: pre-1972 sound recordings first published before 1923 had already lost remedies on 31 December 2021; recordings published 1923–1946 receive 100 years from publication, so those published in or before 1925 are in the public domain from 1 January 2026.
